label: Any number of pharmacies
text: HRSA lets every covered entity use as many contract pharmacies as it likes. Until then most could use one.
The Affordable Care Act opens 340B to more kinds of hospitals: children's, cancer, critical access, rural referral and sole community hospitals.
The HHS Inspector General studies contract pharmacy arrangements at 30 covered entities.

label: New registry system
text: HRSA moves the registry to a new system, 340B OPAIS. The record of ended arrangements this page relies on starts about here.
GAO reports about 20,000 contract pharmacies in 2017, up from about 1,300 in 2010, and asks HRSA to improve its oversight.

label: Drug makers set limits
text: Eli Lilly, then Sanofi, AstraZeneca, Novartis and others limit the 340B price at contract pharmacies.
HHS's General Counsel says drug makers must offer the 340B price at contract pharmacies. The opinion is withdrawn in June 2021.
HRSA tells six drug makers their limits break the 340B statute, and in September refers them to the Inspector General.

label: First state law
text: Arkansas Act 1103 takes effect: drug makers may not limit a covered entity's use of contract pharmacies in the state.
The Third Circuit holds that the federal statute does not require drug makers to deliver to unlimited contract pharmacies.
The Eighth Circuit holds that federal law does not override the Arkansas law.

label: Arkansas law stands
text: The Supreme Court declines to hear the challenge to the Arkansas law. More states follow in 2025.
A federal court in Maine halts HRSA's rebate pilot before it starts; the pilot's notices are set aside in February 2026.
HRSA publishes a revised rebate pilot, set to start on 1 January 2027.
